title: I found my grandmother's photo albums. A man in a gray coat is in every picture, closer each year.
transcript:
I found my grandmother's photo albums. A man in a gray coat is in every picture, closer each year. Grandma kept the albums in a cedar chest with a note on the lid, in her neat handwriting. Never take pictures in the upstairs hallway.

The first album starts in the sixties. Birthday parties, a lake, a new car in the driveway. In the corner of a church picnic photo there's a man in a gray coat, far off by the trees, face turned toward the camera.

He's in the next one too. Closer, by the parking lot. Then at the edge of a wedding, behind the cake table. Every year, every album, a few steps closer. Nobody in the photos ever looks at him.

By the nineteen nineties he's inside the house. A Christmas morning, standing at the foot of the stairs. A birthday, at the kitchen doorway, just behind my mother.

The last picture in the last album is me at seven years old, smiling at the top of the stairs. In the upstairs hallway. He's standing right behind me, close enough to touch.

I put the albums back. Before I left, I took a selfie on the stairs to send my mom, to show her I'd finished packing the house.

I just looked at it.

Both of my hands are in the picture.
